10.1002_aenm.71011: All‐solid‐state sodium batteries (ASSBs) employing halide solid electrolytes (SEs) offer a cost‐effective and energy‐dense alternative to conventional liquid electrolyte systems. However, their high voltage (>4 V vs. Na/Na + ) performance remains limited by interfacial instability between the cathode active material (CAM) and the SE. We present here the electrochemical and interfacial behaviors of crystalline NaAlCl 4 and amorphous sodium–aluminum–oxychloride (NACO) SEs when combined with NaNi 0.5 Mn 0.5 O 2 cathode. While oxygen incorporation in NACO enhances ionic conductivity by nearly three orders of magnitude relative to NaAlCl 4 , it does not improve high‐voltage cycling stability. Cells employing NACO exhibit accelerated capacity fade, increased cell impedance growth, and intrinsic oxygen evolution above 4.5 V vs. Na 3 Sn, as revealed by operando electrochemical mass spectrometry. In contrast, the NaAlCl 4 ‐based cells show no detectable gas release, underscoring their superior high‐voltage stability and safety. Time‐of‐flight secondary‐ion mass spectrometry confirms the formation of Al─O and Ni/Mn─Cl species, respectively, in the SE and CAM, indicating redox‐driven anion exchange that contributes to kinetic hindrance of high‐voltage phase transitions. The findings establish that while oxygen incorporation enhances ionic transport, it can compromise interfacial stability, suggesting pure chloride SEs may offer a more robust and intrinsically safer pathway for developing high‐energy ASSBs.
10.1002_aenm.71569: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) that directly convert natural gas into electricity are promising high‐efficiency energy‐conversion devices, yet conventional Ni‐based anodes suffer from severe carbon deposition and sulfur poisoning, leading to rapid electrode deactivation. Although binary alloying effectively regulates surface reaction pathways and improves anode stability, its development largely relies on experience‐driven trial‐and‐error screening. Here, we propose a rational screening framework that integrates microkinetic analysis with deep neural networks to identify the Ni‐Ga alloy from a vast binary alloy chemical space. Density functional theory confirms that such a Ni‐Ga alloy combines efficient methane activation with intrinsic resistance to carbon deposition. Guided by these predictions, we further construct a nanocomposite electrode with Gd 0.1 Ce 0.9 O 1.95 (GDC)‐encapsulated Ni‐Ga alloys (NiGa‐GDC). Benefiting from alloy‐induced electronic structure modulation and a nanocomposite electrode architecture, the NiGa‐GDC nanocomposite anode exhibits exceptional electrochemical performance and coking resistance. In nearly dry methane fuel (3% H 2 O), a corresponding electrolyte‐supported single cell achieves both high peak power density and durable operation, far outperforming the counterpart Ni‐GDC nanocomposite anode. Moreover, the NiGa‐GDC anode demonstrates remarkable resistance to sulfur poisoning. This study provides a new strategy for developing highly active and durable nickel‐based nanocomposite anodes for the direct utilization of natural gas.
10.1016_j.enconman.2026.122031: Reversible Carnot Batteries are emerging as alternative solutions for renewable energy storage, thanks to their scalability, high energy density, and suitability for seasonal energy storage. Such systems are becoming increasingly competitive for daily energy storage compared to conventional lithium-ion batteries due to their capability to be integrated into multi-energy systems and their lower environmental impact over the entire life cycle. Reversible Carnot Batteries (R-CBs), based on the integration of Heat Pump (HP) and Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC)-based units allows to further reduce the investment costs as the same components are shared. Nevertheless, there is a notable lack of plant analysis of this system when applied on a domestic scale, as well as an assessment of the energy autonomy of the integrated photovoltaic (PV) and R-CB storage system. Indeed, while the literature is rich in thermodynamic and economic analyses, it lacks comprehensive models that consider plant features such as the metallic mass of heat exchangers, piping layout, expander permeability, and mass charge of the working fluid. To fill this gap, a thermo-fluid dynamical model of a reversible Heat Pump–Organic Rankine Cycle (HP–ORC) Carnot Battery for residential applications has been developed and optimized under photovoltaic (PV)-driven operating conditions. The model combines zero-dimensional and one-dimensional approaches to accurately capture both thermodynamic performance and system-level dynamics, including heat exchanger thermal inertia, piping layout, and working fluid mass distribution. Validation against experimental data shows good agreement, with relative errors in the range of 3–6 %. The system is analyzed under winter conditions in central Italy, considering a 60 m 2 PV installation. Results indicate that a thermal energy storage (TES) volume of 8000 L ensures the best trade-off between storage temperature (up to 100 °C) and thermal inertia, in line with those currently adopted in similar applications found in the literature. During discharge, increasing the hot water flow rate from 20 to 30 L·min⁻ 1 results in the power production of a 3 kW ORC unit growing, thus storing up to 4 kWh of electric energy. This ensures that all daily load requirements are fulfilled, with a residual amount of about 1.3 kWh. Another novel aspect highlighted by this work is the assessment of the impact of expander speed on system energy performance. It was observed that reducing the expander speed from 1900 RPM to 1000 RPM increases operating time and improves energy utilization, enabling full load coverage with residual stored energy of 1.5 kWh and peak ORC efficiency close to 7 %. Moreover, the Round-Trip Efficiency (RTE) and exergy efficiency increase by a factor of 2 (34 % and 26 %, respectively) compared to the baseline condition. Therefore, these results open the way for a reversible application of the ORC-based unit as a heat pump to store thermal energy during periods of low electrical energy demand, serving as an alternative to electrochemical storage within batteries.
10.1016_j.ijhydene.2026.157537: Large-scale proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer fleets require supervisory control that increases renewable-hydrogen production while limiting degradation and replacement costs. We propose a degradation-aware coordinated distributed framework combining economic model predictive control (MPC) with soft actor–critic (SAC) reinforcement learning (RL). A degradation model captures voltage rise, state-of-health loss, current limits, and post-knee amplification. Six strategies are evaluated over 20 years for ten heterogeneous stacks using electricity-price and offshore-wind data. The proposed additive–multiplicative modulation (AMM) residual RL–MPC adjusts MPC commands through bounded additive and multiplicative actions under safety constraints. At the PEM-system boundary, AMM achieves the highest net present value (NPV; 12.72 M€), lowest levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH; 5.06 €/kg), 0.006 above-knee fraction, and six replacements. Sensitivities covering economic and model perturbations, forecast error, alternative degradation behavior, fleet heterogeneity, replacement assumptions, and integrated wind–PEM economics support AMM while identifying conditions that change controller rankings.
10.1016_j.memsci.2026.126014: Thin-film composite (TFC) membranes for CO2 separation are often limited by the intrinsic transport resistance of polymeric gutter layers. In this study, uniform, spherical covalent organic framework (COF) nanoparticles were synthesized to serve as a gutter layer in TFC membranes. Poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP) acted as a steric stabilizing agent to regulate particle nucleation and growth, yielding nanoparticles with improved uniformity and smaller size compared to those synthesized without PVP. The closely packed COF nanoparticle gutter layer, deposited on a porous Al2O3 support, suppressed excessive polymer infiltration and enabled the formation of a defect-free, ultrathin polyether block amide (PEBAX) selective layer (~138 nm). The optimized TFC membrane achieved a CO2 permeance of 1,200 GPU with a CO2/N2 selectivity of 43 under single-gas conditions. Under mixed-gas conditions, it maintained a CO2 permeance of 940 GPU with a CO2/N2 selectivity of 47, along with stable operation for over 130 h. These results demonstrate that closely packed, spherical COF nanoparticles serve as an effective and robust gutter layer for enabling an ultrathin polymeric selective layer.
